title: Farouk Jivraj - The Art & Science of Using Alternative Risk Premia (S7E12)

reader_summary.headline: This podcast is for informational purposes only, and should not be relied upon as a basis for investment decisions.
reader_summary.overview: This podcast is for informational purposes only, and should not be relied upon as a basis for investment decisions. In this episode, I speak with Farouk Javrage, Portfolio Manager and head of alternative risk premium at Fidelity Investments Asset Management Solutions Division. After spending nearly a decade decade on the sell side, Farouk joined Fadley in 2021 with the goal of building out an alternative risk premium platform.

key_points.text: After spending nearly a decade decade on the sell side.
key_points.evidence_quote: After spending nearly a decade decade on the sell side, Farouk joined Fadley in 2021 with the goal of building out an alternative risk premium platform, tapping into the best of what both the cell side QIS desks have to offer and what can be built in-house.

key_points.text: We spend the majority of the conversation peeling apart the layers of Farouk's five-step process for implementing alternative risk premium strategies.
key_points.evidence_quote: We spend the majority of the conversation peeling apart the layers of Farouk's five-step process for implementing alternative risk premium strategies.

key_points.text: He shares his thoughts on how to classify different premium, why thoughtfully constructed peer groups are an important evaluation tool.
key_points.evidence_quote: He shares his thoughts on how to classify different premium, why thoughtfully constructed peer groups are an important evaluation tool, how to go about selecting specific strategies, how to construct portfolios of alternative risk premium and the actual rubber rubber meets road implementation practicalities.

key_points.text: Please enjoy my conversation with Farooch Javraj.
key_points.evidence_quote: Please enjoy my conversation with Farooch Javraj.

thesis: The speaker argues that while studying, selling, and investing in strategies share technical commonalities, they require distinctly different mindsets and experiences. He emphasizes that the field is fundamentally about long-term investing and managing the psychology required to achieve long-run objectives.
